result.answer:
Verdict: REFUTED

**Evidence against the claim:**
- The paper adopts QANet as its base QA model and states outright that "there are completely no recurrent networks in QANet" [S:d5988bab994b#2].
- The absence of recurrence is given as a reason for choosing QANet: it makes training "5x faster than BiDAF" at the same SQuAD performance [S:d5988bab994b#2].

**Evidence for the claim:** none in the supplied passages.

**Limitation:** the passages do not enumerate QANet's internal encoder/decoder components (e.g., self-attention or convolution blocks); they only assert the absence of recurrent networks [S:d5988bab994b#2].

citations.title: Mitigating the Impact of Speech Recognition Errors on Spoken
citations.text:
The used architecture of the QA model is briefly summarized below. Here we choose QANet BIBREF2
as the base model due to the following reasons: 1) it achieves the second best performance on SQuAD,
and 2) since there are completely no recurrent networks in QANet, its training speed is 5x faster than
BiDAF BIBREF17 when reaching the same performance on SQuAD.
